# Hyper UI source snapshot

The snapshot script orders More's Most used items as Chat, Participants, Agenda, Notes, and Transcript so the prototype's implemented nested panels appear first. It preserves the original row components and actions.

Only the visible panel's call control uses the active tone and expanded state. Chat and People clear More's active state; selecting More from either nested view returns to the More list.

The snapshot script changes the call controls' 18px (`size-4.5`) primary icon tokens to 20px (`size-5`), including media toggles, reaction hover states, More, and compact controls. Device-picker carets retain their original sizing. The local Figma video-off adapter uses the same 20px icon frame.

Participant tile fallback avatars use a 96px size with Hyper's corresponding 24px initials on desktop and tablet viewports (768px and above), and 80px avatars with 20px initials on mobile. These sizes are scoped through the prototype stylesheet. Their original avatar components and speaking ripples remain intact.

The layout control retains its Dynamic label and original appearance, but its dropdown menu is omitted for now. Activating it does not change participant views or the stage layout.

At desktop and tablet viewport widths (768px and above), tile name labels use 10px inline padding and 6px block padding. Their 8px edge offsets and corner radii apply at every viewport size.

The mobile top bar keeps the original compact recording island in its center slot. Equal 88px side columns center it independently of the logo/layout and Invite/Search groups; the title truncates on narrow previews. The mobile layout trigger retains its layout icon and right-hand chevron at 32px high. Invite uses the original 32px icon-button sizing with `HugeUserAdd01Stroke`. Desktop retains its full logo, layout label, participant stack, and text Invite action.

Audio and video device-menu settings actions use Hyper's original `HugeSettings02Stroke`, matching the footer's `HugeSettings02Duotone` outline without its fill layer. The snapshot script preserves this scoped icon substitution.

The mobile preview spans the available footer width. React sits at the leading edge, More at the trailing edge, and the microphone/camera/leave controls share a centered group with 12px gaps. The outer row uses space-between with equal-width edge actions, retaining Hyper's original button components and sizes.

The original `MeetingReactionStream` is composed into the local participant tile's `media` slot, clipped to that tile so sent reactions stay within Jon's video area. The reaction picker uses a 16px popup radius through `contentClassName`; the host stylesheet gives its choices 8px corners and removes their hover translation.

The call-control action model follows `MeetingCallControlsInteractiveExample` in the supplied `call-controls.demo-fixtures.tsx`: source tooltip copy for each state, accent tones for Share and Captions, and panel-active tones for Chat, People, and More. Desktop controls and mobile sheet actions share the same state and handlers. Share and Captions simulate toggles; Settings and Access expose selectable placeholder states; Chat and People open their nested More panel views. Only one panel action is selected at a time. Device-menu settings actions select the same Settings state. Placeholder controls use `aria-pressed` rather than announcing an absent expanded panel.

At the user's request, the tile name overlay imports Hyper's `HugeMicOff02Duotone` under its existing muted-icon name, matching the microphone call control. The snapshot script preserves this import substitution; tile sizing and mute-state behavior remain unchanged.

This is the subset of the user-supplied `hyper-ui` repository needed by the Hyper meeting case study. `manifest.json` records the upstream revision and a SHA-256 hash of both each original file and its local snapshot.

The component implementations, icons, design tokens, and interactions come from Hyper UI. Imports are rewritten to relative paths so this repository builds without the sibling checkout or private registry credentials. The icon entrypoint includes only the required exports. The upstream tiles entry references an absent `LucideVideoOff` export; the local facade maps that legacy name to Hyper's existing `HyperVideoOffDuotone` asset. Type exports use `export type` for Next.js isolated modules.

The meeting's `MeetingVideoOffIcon` is a user-requested Figma replacement from file `7p0SO1BOGmnOaB0CiQZhKk`, node `588:3679`. The snapshot script routes that leaf to the site's adapter in `components/hyper-meeting/icons/`; both original and adapted hashes remain in the manifest. The adapter renders the exported SVG in `public/prototypes/hyper-meeting/icons/video-off.svg`, preserving its natural dimensions and centered placement within the 24×24 Figma frame, displayed at 20px. Only the exported palette is changed from `#262626` to the prototype's existing `#FF6467` red, as requested. The host stylesheet removes the split pill's horizontal SVG nudge for the microphone and camera toggles so their icons stay centered in both states.

The stylesheet retains Hyper's tokens, utilities, and motion. Imports and source scans for unused Markdown, AI, and shimmer integrations are omitted. It is loaded only by `/prototypes/hyper-meeting`, inside the case study's iframe, so its Tailwind theme cannot change the portfolio page.

The host stylesheet overrides the fullscreen app's `overscroll-behavior` with native vertical chaining on the iframe's `html` and `body`. Scrolling can continue into the surrounding case study, while panels consume their own scroll until reaching an edge.

`fonts/` retains the Latin variable Inter font from the supplied docs app's `@fontsource-variable/inter` 5.3.0 installation and its license. The prototype loads it under the existing `Inter` family token so the theme uses the intended typeface rather than a system fallback. Font assets are hashed in the manifest and refreshed by the snapshot script.

`tile-layouts/` retains the supplied, installed `@hypervideo/tile-layouts` 2.0.1 package, including its license, and powers the actual participant layout calculations.

To refresh from an available checkout, run from the personal site root:

```sh
node scripts/snapshot-hyper-ui.mjs /absolute/path/to/hyper-ui
```

Keep application state, sample participants, and compositions in `components/hyper-meeting/`. Keep the reusable device viewer in `components/prototype/`. Do not restyle or replace the source components to extend a composition; update the snapshot from the design system when its implementation changes.

The top bar uses the supplied `meeting-ui/primitives/top-bar.tsx` directly. Its desktop slots retain the original 16px group spacing and 32px control height. The logo and layout trigger follow `layouts/meeting-shell.demo-fixtures.tsx`, including the trigger's native padding, icon sizing, and gap. The right slot uses the supplied `AvatarStack` and `AvatarStackItem` components for all four sample participants, with the header example's 24px avatar size and the stack's native 6px overlap and masks. Invite and Search remain grouped 8px apart, 16px after the stack. The stack opens the same People panel as the footer. Compact headers retain the recording island and essential controls while hiding the desktop stack. Search stays an enabled placeholder button without opening a dialog; Invite copies the case study link and keeps its label unchanged. The official shadcn/ui Base Nova Toast component confirms the successful copy inside the prototype iframe, including the recording-island Copy invite link action. Repeated copies refresh one toast; clipboard failures show an error with a browser-address fallback. The toaster is mounted only on the prototype route. Its default shadcn neutral theme, radius scale, shadow, and shadcn action/close buttons are scoped to its viewport so Hyper’s tokens do not alter its appearance. It uses the default shadcn viewport positioning at every size.

The recording state uses the original `MeetingIslandDesktop`, `MeetingIslandMobile`, and animated `MeetingRecordingIcon` from `surfaces/meeting-island/`. Its recording status is enabled in this sample meeting. The local composition owns the elapsed clock and editable title, preserving both when the viewer changes device sizes. The original desktop island supplies the title menu, recording tooltip, and timer; its Rename, Copy invite link, and End meeting actions use local meeting state. Rename delegates through the source onRename callback to a local composition of Hyper's Dialog, Input, Label, and Button components. Save commits a trimmed nonempty name; Cancel, Escape, and the close button discard the draft and return focus to the meeting menu trigger. The snapshot script preserves the Copy invite link label. Mobile uses Hyper's compact logo and centered island, with icon-only layout, Invite, and Search controls to preserve space.

The stage uses the original `MeetingCallStageRoot`, responsive `MeetingCallStageMain`, `MeetingCallContentFrame`, and `MeetingTileGridViewport`. The shell owns the single 16px stage gutter; the main surface uses `fullBleed` to avoid doubling it. `useMeetingTileLayout` retains Hyper's 8px tile gap, sizing, focus/pin layout, and divider. The host stylesheet sets name labels 8px from the bottom/left and menu buttons 8px from the top/right, both with 8px corners. Menu buttons appear on tile hover or keyboard focus and remain visible while their menu is open; devices without hover retain visible menu targets. A local simulated conversation cycles all four participants through the original `isSpeaking` state, with pauses and brief overlaps. Hyper's existing tile outline and avatar ripples show each speaker. Muting the local microphone suppresses that participant's speaking state, and the sequence pauses in background tabs.

Call controls follow `apps/docs/src/examples/call/controls.tsx`, using the original `CallControls` parts and shell slots. Desktop uses the three action groups; compact widths use video, audio, reactions, leave, and More. At the user's request, the compact More trigger composes Hyper's original `DrawerTrigger`, `MobilePreviewButton`, and `MeetingMoreIcon` so it matches the desktop More button while opening the action sheet. That sheet includes nested device selection and access to the meeting's More panel. Device names follow Hyper's fixtures, selections use local state, and the original `AudioLevelMeter` shows the reference's fixed sample signal. All call controls and regular More panel items are enabled, including placeholder actions without destinations. Only Coming soon entries remain disabled. Call-control popovers and drawers retain the source radii along with the buttons in the main bar.

The local composition adds an intermediate desktop layout matching the supplied compact control-bar reference. Below 1100px of control-container width, Captions and People hide, retaining Settings/Access, Audio/Video/Share/React/Leave, and Chat/More in their original groups. At 768px of available control width, those groups fit with 32px gaps; below that the original five-action mobile preview takes over. Buttons and split media controls keep Hyper's original small sizing, and an open More panel uses the original `panelActive` tone. Named container queries adapt to the remaining meeting column when a side panel opens, independently of the iframe viewport.

The host composition places the original `MeetingSidePanelRoot` beside the entire meeting column so it spans the header, stage, and controls. The case study's requested 8px button radius is scoped in the prototype stylesheet; call controls retain their original Hyper radii.


People and Chat are local compositions of the original `meeting-ui/surfaces/participants/` and `chat-ui/` production components, using the People Panel (`pIU0iGy2dcot2b822Meju8`, node `2805:27356`) and Chat Panel (`bAUaF3c0AlJQ9gpOWA4ad8`, node `4781:11787`) Figma references for their nested headers, density, and scrolling. They share More's single full-height, 400px desktop sidebar and inset mobile overlay. Back returns focus to the corresponding More item; Close and Escape dismiss the sidebar. The mobile overlay keeps keyboard focus inside the visible panel, with the meeting column inert behind it.

People uses the existing four participants, Host and Members groups, native search/collapsible sections, media status indicators, and participant menus connected to the stage's focus and pin states. Waiting and Invited remain empty rather than introducing extra participants. The People panel omits Invite and lets search span the available width. Participant overflow menus follow People Panel node `2805:29715`, with a participant-name header, three action groups, a 240 × 220px popup, 12px outer corners, and the five original 16px Figma icon exports in `public/prototypes/hyper-meeting/icons/participant-menu/`. Pin/maximize, media toggles, and removal affect local meeting state shared by the stage, People rows, and avatar stack; removing yourself leaves the prototype meeting. Removing another participant moves keyboard focus to a remaining participant or section trigger. Rejoining restores the sample roster and media states. Participant rows follow Figma nodes `2805:27396` and `2805:28349`: full-width square-edged rows with 16px left/8px right padding, 8px vertical padding, 24px avatars, medium 14px/20px names, 32px status/action slots separated by 4px, and an input/30 hover fill. The existing microphone and camera icons remain intact; muted microphones use the same red palette and opacity as camera-off indicators. Section headers show plain 14px medium labels with counts in parentheses. A far-right original Hyper Collapsible trigger uses the same 32px ghost icon Button as the sidebar Close action, with a 16px chevron indicating expansion. Each trigger has an explicit Expand/Collapse label and retains native accordion keyboard behavior within an 8px-padded row. Chat uses a fictional design-review history from those participants, their existing avatar colors, original message/reaction primitives, and Hyper's Editate composer with formatting, links, lists, code, emoji, and participant mentions. Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a line break. Messages, reactions, drafts, and search survive nested navigation and panel closure for the current meeting. Message reactions follow Chat Panel nodes `4781:17714` and `4781:17032`: 32px reaction pills with an adjacent add button, a full-width hover fill, and a 36px floating toolbar ordered as 👍, 💯, 🔥, then a divider and custom emoji. Original Hyper message/reaction, Tooltip, Popover, and emoji-picker components implement the interactions; original Figma face-plus exports preserve the 16px footer and 20px toolbar glyphs. Reactions and counts are isolated by message, toggle once per viewer, and persist across panel navigation. Touch devices also expose the add button on messages without existing reactions. The composer stays below the independently scrolling history. No chat service or meeting backend is contacted.

The message scroller's default icon/label fragment is wrapped in a keyed `display: contents` span by the snapshot script. This avoids React's missing-key warning during the upstream render-prop merge without changing the component's layout or behavior. The composer snapshot also reads formatting from the preceding text leaf at a collapsed caret, so Bold, Italic, and other active marks persist beyond the first typed character. These compatibility adjustments preserve Hyper’s components and visual design; all original and adapted file hashes remain recorded in the manifest.


The chat composer matches Figma `bAUaF3c0AlJQ9gpOWA4ad8`, nodes `4781:11876` (pinned formatting) and `4781:12545` (inline selection). Hyper's original composer, toolbar actions, Popover, emoji picker, and Attachment components remain the implementation. A local CSS module supplies the reference's 8px padding/corners, 28px controls, 4px control gaps, 14px/20px text, inside stroke, plain blue mentions, and compact 116px single-line height. The Text formatting action toggles the pinned toolbar. With it hidden, selecting text opens the same actions above the selection in a 12px-radius popover that stays inside the preview viewport. Alt+F10 moves focus to formatting controls; arrows navigate them. Escape dismisses the selection toolbar while keeping Chat open. The input grows with multiline content before scrolling internally.

The original composer glyphs are exported from the exact Figma instances into `public/prototypes/hyper-meeting/icons/chat-composer/`. Each retains its 16px frame and optical placement; CSS masks recolor the same SVGs for hover/active/disabled states. The directory's manifest records source nodes and SHA-256 hashes. Attachment selection, removal, local sending, and downloading use browser-local File objects; no files are uploaded. Empty Send is disabled, and selecting a file allows attachment-only messages.
